newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Most Irish want law to curb tide of refugees - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Irish want law to curb tide of refugees - poll.

text.p: Most Irish people want new laws to curb a tide of refugees which has brought a wave of central European people begging on Dublin street corners, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.
The IMS poll for the Irish Independent said 56 per cent of a sample 1,115 voters wanted new laws against refugees and only 29 per cent of people opposed them.
It was a response to a sudden influx of refugees, many from Romania, former Yugsolavia and elsewhere, which began in the past few months and which has worried police and the government.
The government has suggested that there many refugees may have entered Ireland illegally by paying gangs operating in Britain and Europe to smuggle them into Ireland.
Police were called to a Health Board centre in Dublin this month when a large number of refugees demanding social welfare benefits overwhelmed staff.
According to official figures, only 39 people applied for asylum in Ireland in 1992 but the number this year so far is 1,200 and up to 6,000 may be expected, officials say.
Two groups of Romanians were prevented from sailing to Ireland from French ports in recent weeks when police discovered that their papers were not in order.
Ireland has an open-door policy for refugees and asylum seekers and the government says it is proud of its record towards genuine cases.
